//: UNBREAKABLE SHAFT WALL.  This is the load-bearing design decision of SCP-087 in CDDA: the shaft cannot be escaped by force.  Two things make it unbreakable, and BOTH are required:
//2: (1) There is NO 'bash' block.  src/map.cpp:4861 checks `if( fd.first->bash_info && !fd.first->indestructible )` before bashing terrain - with no bash_info, bashing is simply not possible.  Do NOT copy-from t_rock: t_rock HAS a bash block (data/json/furniture_and_terrain/terrain-walls.json:1992-2000, str_min 100) and is therefore deliberately breakable.  That is the opposite of what this mod needs.
//3: (2) There are NO 'MINEABLE' or 'DIGGABLE' flags (src/mapdata.cpp:204, 220).  Without them a pickaxe or jackhammer has no valid target, so the player cannot mine out either.
//4: Together these mean the only exits are: the seam, the fake up-stairs, starvation/dehydration, debug, and the loop-13 ejection.  There is no 'the stone resists' message because there is nothing to resist - the option never appears.
//5: TILES (looks_like).  These terrains ship no art of their own; they point at the closest base-game ids instead, which gives them real sprites in any tileset that has those ids, with no images to maintain and no sprite-index bookkeeping.
//6: WHY THIS IS SAFE, VERIFIED: 'looks_like' is read ONLY by the tile drawer - a grep of src/ finds it exclusively in src/cata_tiles.cpp (find_tile_looks_like at :1965, the terrain/furniture/monster cases at :2018-2026, the overmap case at :2033).  It is cosmetic and cannot copy flags or data, so it cannot leak GOES_UP onto t_scp_087_stairs_none or change what any tile does in play.  It is also a fallback: if a tileset ever ships art for our own ids, that art wins automatically.
//7: TARGETS, each verified to exist as a real game object: t_concrete_wall (data/json/furniture_and_terrain/terrain-walls.json:228), t_thconc_floor (terrain-floors-indoor.json:4), t_stairs_up / t_stairs_down (terrain-zlevel-transitions.json:143 / :120), t_door_metal_c / t_door_metal_o (terrain-doors.json:2509 / :2741).  Terrains defined with copy-from inherit the parent's looks_like, which is deliberate in two places: t_scp_087_landing and t_scp_087_seam inherit the floor's look (so the seam is genuinely indistinguishable from the step around it), and t_scp_087_stairs_none inherits the up-stairs look (so the sealed way up still looks like a working staircase).
name: painted concrete wall
description: A wall of poured concrete, painted a faded institutional green and scuffed at shoulder height by decades of people squeezing past.  The paint is the only thing that suggests this was ever meant to be seen by anyone.  There is no give in it at all.

//: Shaft floor at the head of a flight.  Ordinary to look at, impossible to remove.  The description carries the article's detail that there are no lighting fixtures and no windows anywhere in SCP-087 - the darkness is structural, not an oversight.
name: concrete step
description: A poured concrete step, worn smooth and slightly dished in the middle by the passage of many feet.  The angle is wrong for a building this size - too steep, and it turns back on itself every thirteen steps.  There are no lights and no windows.  There is nowhere for light to come from.

//: The landing at each turn.  From the article: 'Stairs descend on a 38 degree angle for 13 steps before reaching a semicircular platform of approximately 3 meters in diameter.'  Purely a floor variant so the landings read differently from the flights underfoot.
name: landing
description: A semicircular concrete landing, about three meters across, where the stair reverses direction.  The surface is uneven in a way that is hard to look at directly - as though it has been poured, worn away, and poured again more times than the building has stood.

//: Roof tile.  CDDA requires a SUPPORTS_ROOF terrain to reference a roof.  t_scp_087_roof is deliberately solid concrete, not open air: this shaft is indoors at every level, which is what makes it pitch dark without a lamp.
//2: TILES: UltimateCataclysm ships no roof or ceiling ids at all (t_flat_roof, t_roof and t_metal_roof are all absent from its tile_config), so there is nothing roof-shaped to point at.  This points at the concrete wall instead, which reads as a bare concrete slab if the tile is ever drawn.  In practice it never is - the player is always underneath it, and CDDA only draws the level the player is standing on - so this is completeness rather than appearance.
name: concrete ceiling
description: A slab of bare concrete.  There is no wiring in it, no conduit, and no hatch.  Nothing above this has ever connected to anything below it.

//: THE CONTAINMENT BOUNDARY.  This is the tile at the mouth of the shaft, where the stairwell meets the surface closet.  It uses MON_AVOID_STRICT, which src/monmove.cpp:172-174 enforces inside the monster movement path:
//2: if( here->has_flag( ter_furn_flag::TFLAG_MON_AVOID_STRICT, p ) ) { return false; }
//3: So SCP-087-1 physically cannot path onto this tile, and therefore cannot leave the shaft - the user's requirement that it never escapes.  It is TRANSPARENT and passable for the PLAYER, which is the whole point: the precedent is data/json/furniture_and_terrain/netherum/terrain_labyrinth_any.json, which puts MON_AVOID_STRICT on an EMPTY_SPACE tile the player walks through but monsters refuse.
//4: The practical consequence, as agreed: the surface landing is a genuine safe zone.  You can stand at the mouth with SCP-087-1 pressed against the boundary and it cannot reach you.  That is what makes the loop-13 ejection meaningfully different from death, and it makes the loop-5 point of no return bite - you remember being safe, and now you are not.
name: shaft mouth
description: The top of the stairwell, where the concrete gives way to a painted doorframe.  The transition is abrupt - a few steps down and the building stops making sense, the staircase turning back on itself into a dark that the light does not seem to reach into.  Whatever is down there does not come up here.

//: The descent within the shaft.  Deliberately NOT the threshold id: monsters must be able to use these stairs, because SCP-087-1 has to be able to follow the player down.  Only the top mouth tile carries MON_AVOID_STRICT - that is the containment boundary, and it exists exactly once, at the surface end of the shaft.
//2: TILES: the base game's t_stairs_down renders in UltimateCataclysm as grey treads descending into a black void (sprite checked directly) - the right read for the top of an unnaturally deep stairwell.  t_scp_087_threshold points at the same id, since it is the mouth of that same descent.
name: stairs down
description: A flight of concrete steps leading further down.  The treads are dished in the middle and the angle is steeper than anything a building inspector would have signed off on.

//: The way up, before loop 5.  Identical to the threshold but flagged GOES_UP, so ascending returns the player to the surface closet.  Deliberately a SEPARATE id from t_scp_087_threshold: after loop 5 the EOC swaps this terrain for t_scp_087_stairs_none, because ordinary stairs cannot lie and the 'way up is gone' state has to be represented as different terrain.
//2: TILES: points at the base game's t_stairs_up.  t_scp_087_stairs_none COPY-FROMs this entry and declares no looks_like of its own, so after loop 5 the dead staircase inherits exactly this sprite - which is the whole point: the sealed way up has to keep looking like a staircase you could still climb.  That inheritance is safe precisely because looks_like is cosmetic (read only by src/cata_tiles.cpp) and cannot carry the GOES_UP flag across.
name: stairs up
description: A flight of concrete steps leading up toward the closet.  The paint on the walls is the same institutional green as the floor above, which is briefly reassuring.

//: The way up, after loop 5 - the point of no return.  There is NO GOES_UP flag, so pressing the ascend key does nothing at all: the stairs are simply a dead surface.  This is the honest way to represent 'the way back is gone' in CDDA; the alternative (letting it teleport you somewhere else) would be a lie the player can feel.
//2: The description is the only tell, and it is meant to be ambiguous: the stairs look completely normal.  That is the horror - not a dramatic collapse, but a door that quietly stopped being a door.
name: stairs up
description: A flight of concrete steps leading up toward the closet.  The paint is the same institutional green.  It is a perfectly ordinary staircase, and it no longer goes anywhere.

//: THE SEAM.  A plain-looking step at the bottom of the deepest authored flight.  Stepping onto it trigger-teleports the player to a layout-identical landing near the top of the shaft, so the descent appears to continue forever even though the map has looped.  It is a trap rather than terrain logic because traps fire on entry without any input from the player, which is exactly the behaviour needed - the loop must happen TO the player, not be chosen by them.
name: concrete step
description: Another step down.  Nothing about it is worth a second look.

//: THE REINFORCED STEEL DOOR.  From the article: 'The doorway leading to SCP-087 is constructed of reinforced steel with an electro-release lock mechanism...'  The article's lock is deliberately NOT modelled: the door simply opens.  The horror is what is inside, not a lockpicking minigame stood between the player and the anomaly.  It is still a heavy steel door in flavour - and still slow to smash - it is just not a gatekeeper.
//2: WHAT MAKES IT OPENABLE: 'open' points at t_scp_087_door_o, and the DOOR flag marks it as a real door.  map::open_door acts on ter.open (src/map.cpp:5290-5307) - with no 'open' link, pressing 'o' does nothing at all, which is exactly what the earlier locked version did.
//3b: LOCKED / PICKABLE / lockpick_result / examine_action 'locked_object' - with any of those present the examine menu still offers the lock minigame.
//3c: OPENCLOSE_INSIDE - that flag makes map::open_door refuse when the opener is standing OUTSIDE (src/map.cpp:5291: `if( has_flag( OPENCLOSE_INSIDE, p ) && !inside ) { return false; }`, and callers pass `!here.is_outside( the opener's position )`).  On an exterior door it blocks the one interaction we want.  It is the single flag the base game's own t_door_metal_interior_locked exists to remove.
//3d: TRANSPARENT - this is a windowless steel door, and the base game's closed metal door is opaque.  Opaque also means you cannot see into the closet from outside, which is the point.
//4: NOT on MON_AVOID_STRICT: the door is the 'outside' face, and SCP-087-1 is contained by the t_scp_087_threshold tile one step inside instead.  Leaving the door open therefore still holds the anomaly in.
name: reinforced steel door
description: A windowless steel door, painted to match the janitorial closet around it.  The handle is set into a heavy latch plate, and a thin cable runs from the frame to a sealed box near the top.  Someone has painted over the locking mechanism so many times it is almost flush with the door.  The latch moves, if you put your weight behind it.

//: THE DOORWAY, OPEN.  Only ever created by opening t_scp_087_door above, and shaped after the base game's t_door_metal_o (src data/json/furniture_and_terrain/terrain-doors.json:2741) so an open doorway behaves like every other open door in the game - passable, transparent, and closeable again.
//2: IT CARRIES THE DOORWAY TRAP.  There is no engine event for 'a door was opened' (event.h has no door event, and map::open_door exposes no data hook), so the 'you open the door and there is nothing inside' beat hangs off the OPEN DOORWAY TILE instead - the step the player takes the instant after opening it.  The mechanics are the ones the seam already relies on: a built-in terrain trap resolves from the terrain itself (src/map.cpp:7065-7068) and is NOT consumed by trapfunc::eocs's here.remove_trap (src/trapfunc.cpp:508, which only clears the submap trap field), so it re-arms for every later visit.  AVATAR_ONLY keeps NPCs and SCP-087-1 from firing the player's beat; see traps/scp_087_traps.json.
name: open steel door
description: The same steel door, standing open.  Through the gap the closet is only concrete and dark - whatever the cable over the frame was wired to, it was not a light.
